processes.title: Sell from Stock with Advanced Down Payment
processes.memory_hook: Collect cash before final delivery billing, but keep the sales flow intact.

sap_scope_items.label: Sell from Stock with Down Payment Processing

processes.business_intent: Extend sell-from-stock with down payment requests and later settlement against customer invoices.

control_plane.why: determines whether the sales item participates in ADP
links requested/received down payments to final settlement

data_hinges.changes: when and how much is requested
what can be settled against the final invoice
maximum relevant down-payment amount and settlement context

impact_summary: Adds a cash/receivables control layer before final delivery-related billing without turning the sales order into a separate financial process.
constraints: ADP cannot be combined with some billing features such as retroactive billing or reference billing plans.
Legal and tax handling is localization-sensitive.
lead_questions: Is the down payment a commercial requirement or a legal/tax requirement?
What should block fulfillment if payment is missing?
How is settlement traced to the final invoice?

processes.title: Milestone Billing with Advanced Down Payment
processes.memory_hook: Bill the project in stages; collect down payments against the same staged logic.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Order Processing with Milestone Billing

processes.business_intent: Combine order-related milestone billing with advanced down payment requests for trading goods, non-stock products, or services where supported.

control_plane.control: billing plan type and milestone dates

control_plane.why: determines which sales items can use the process

data_hinges.changes: commercial exposure and remaining billable value

impact_summary: The process shifts the commercial clock from delivery events to agreed billing milestones, with down payments settled into that schedule.
constraints: The exact supported item categories and localization behavior are release-sensitive.
lead_questions: What business event proves a milestone?
What prevents the final invoice from ignoring earlier down payments?

processes.title: Sales Bill of Material / Sales Kit
processes.memory_hook: One sellable product can explode into a main item and components.
processes.business_intent: Sell a structured product while deciding whether pricing, inventory and delivery are controlled mainly by the main item or by its components.

control_plane.why: keeps processing mainly on the main item; classic standard main-item category is TAQ
moves processing to the component level; classic standard main-item category is TAP
uses document type, item category group, item usage and higher-level item category to determine main and subitem behavior
can synchronize dates and quantities across dependent components

data_hinges.changes: which subitems appear in the sales order and their quantity ratio

data_hinges.data: item category group ERLA or LUMF
data_hinges.changes: whether the main item or components own pricing, inventory and delivery behavior
subitem item-category determination and follow-on behavior
the correlated delivery date when the kit should move together
whether the order remains only a sales structure or also creates customer-specific production demand

impact_summary: A Sales BOM controls how the product structure is sold and executed in the sales document.
A Production BOM controls how the product is manufactured. They can share product structure, but they answer different business questions.
With an MTO strategy, the sales-order requirement can drive planning and production while the Sales BOM still controls the commercial main-item/subitem structure.
One missing component can move the promise for the complete kit when delivery-group correlation is active.
constraints: ERLA and LUMF are item category groups, not sales item categories.
Do not assume that a Sales BOM automatically means make-to-order production.
Delivery-group correlation has prerequisites and does not reconcile every partial or fixed-quantity scenario.
Main-item and subitem changes can affect pricing, ATP, delivery, copying and document flow; test changes after the sales order already exists.
Sales-kit support in advanced intercompany has additional boundaries.
lead_questions: Where should pricing sit: main item or components?
Is this only a sales structure, or must the demand also trigger MTO production?
Should one missing component block the complete kit?
What should happen when the BOM changes after the sales order was created?

modes.title: Main-item processing
modes.memory: Main item owns the commercial control; components mainly explain the structure.

modes.title: Component-level processing
modes.memory: Components carry the operational sales and delivery behavior.

item_patterns.note: Main-item processing in a standard order.
Header carries the structure while pricing and logistics are handled on subitems.
The exact subitem category depends on higher-level item category, component item category group and configuration.

relations.why: Main and subitem behavior is resolved through item-category determination.
The resulting item categories influence schedule lines, requirements and delivery relevance.
With an MTO strategy, the sales-order requirement becomes customer-specific supply and production.
Assembly processing can create a production-side object directly from the sales order.
